```{r}
#First we activate the needed packages.
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)
library(knitr)
```


```{r}
library(tidyverse)

#Then we load the data.

DKmonarch <- read_csv("/Users/Aruuk/Desktop/kings.csv", na ="NULL")
DKmonarch
```

```{r}
#We use a pipe to add a new row called duration: 
DKmonarch <- DKmonarch %>%
  mutate(duration = End_year - Start_year)

```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)

#We make a pipe where we plot duration on the y-axis and birth on the x-axis:  
DKmonarch %>%
ggplot(aes(x = Birth_year , y = duration)) +
geom_point() +
geom_smooth()
```
This leave us with the obviously conclusion that the monarchs born later in the
century have a longer duration time. This is obviously since the average age for 
a person has gotten longer throughout the centuries.
